text: Bitcoin Core is rewriting its security policy for a world where $BTC bugs can be found with a single AI prompt. The project will now backport fixes and cut releases immediately for flaws flagged as “easily discoverable,” moving away from the long embargoes that once gave developers time to patch quietly. The change targets a new threat model: attackers using AI to surface vulnerabilities quickly, before a slow disclosure process can contain them. Under the revised approach, easily discoverable bugs get fast-tracked fixes and releases rather than extended secrecy. That shift matters because embargoes are meant to protect users while a fix is prepared. But if AI makes discovery cheap and fast, a long embargo may only delay defense while the flaw is already exposed. text: According to Jin10, British Finance Minister John Healey filled a £5 billion shortfall in the defense investment plan in his first budget. Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer had not fully set out the defense spending plan, leaving Healey and current Prime Minister Andy Burnham with a £5 billion funding gap when they took it over. Healey said the budget fully funds the plan, including by reprioritizing capital spending across government departments, fulfilling a commitment he and the prime minister had made. He has not yet said whether the UK will raise defense spending to 3% of GDP by 2030. In June, he resigned as defense minister after then-Prime Minister Starmer refused to make that commitment.

text: SK hynix (NASDAQ: $SKHY) Jumps 8% as Record Q3 Revenue Tops KRW 100 Trillion. SK hynix shares jumped more than 8% in Wednesday’s premarket trading after the South Korean chipmaker reported record third-quarter revenue of KRW 104.62 trillion, up 328% from a year earlier. Operating profit rose 632% to KRW 83.33 trillion, while its operating margin hit a record 80%. Both results beat analyst estimates. The company credited strong demand for AI-related memory chips and rising memory prices for its growth. SK hynix also began mass production and shipments of its next-generation HBM4 memory. In addition, it plans to return approximately KRW 100 trillion to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks for fiscal 2026. #Crypto

Specifically, the XRP Cost Basis data reveals that approximately 2.5 billion tokens last changed hands around $1.61, which could create a potential resistance level whenever the price tries to rebound above current levels. XRP Cost Basis Heatmap Shows Supply Clusters For context, the Cost Basis Distribution Heatmap tracks the prices at which XRP last changed hands on the blockchain. text: Elliott Wave analyst V has warned that #Cardano has yet to reach its final bottom, raising the possibility of another decline if ADA breaks below a key technical support level. V identified Cardano as a strong candidate for a cryptocurrency that could establish a new low. Notably, he emphasized that a breakdown below the lower boundary of its ascending price channel could strengthen this bearish outlook. Cardano Risks Falling to $0.14 V’s accompanying chart shows Cardano trading within an ascending channel since it reached a low of $0.1384 in June 2026. The pattern consists of two upward-sloping trendlines, with the lower boundary providing support during previous pullbacks. However, ADA has recently approached this lower trendline after retreating from the $0.28 region in early October. At the time of the analysis, it traded around $0.217, placing it near a critical support area. Moreov

text: South Korea may delay its crypto tax again. The country's 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year is set to start on January 1, 2027. But lawmakers, including the ruling Democratic Party, are pushing a bill that would tie the start date to Korea's first crypto data exchange under the OECD reporting framework, which would likely mean 2029. It would be the fourth delay of a tax first passed in 2020. The government's official position is still that it starts on schedule, and any change needs a law amendment before January 1. #SouthKorea #CryptoTax #Regulation #CryptoNews

text: Bitcoin Core is changing how it handles security bugs because of AI. Developers updated the project's security policy so that bugs AI tools can easily find get fixed and released straight away across all maintained versions, instead of being held back under the usual long embargo. Their reasoning: AI models make these bugs much easier to discover, so quietly sitting on a patch no longer protects anyone. A smart adjustment to keep the network safe. $BTC #Bitcoin #BitcoinCore #Security #CryptoNews

text: Ethereum researchers want much faster settlement. A new proposal would cut the time for Ethereum transactions to become final from about 16 minutes to around 4 minutes. text: Ethereum's next upgrade hits a delay. Developers postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade's final test on the Hoodi testnet after auditors found its gas pricing changes could break 13 existing smart contracts. No new date has been set, which puts the end-of-2026 target for mainnet at risk. Good to see security being prioritized over speed. Shipping a broken upgrade would cost far more than a short delay. $ETH #Ethereum #Glamsterdam #CryptoNews

creator: Calc Media
text: Solana just shipped its biggest upgrade in years. The Alpenglow upgrade went live on October 21, replacing the consensus system Solana has run since 2020. According to core developer Anza, it cuts the time for a transaction to become final from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds under normal network conditions. Near-instant finality is a big deal for payments, trading and DeFi apps built on Solana. $SOL #Solana #Alpenglow #CryptoNews

text: JPMorgan's deposit token is now live on Ethereum mainnet. JPM Coin (ticker JPMD) went live on Ethereum on October 19 for approved institutional clients, joining its existing deployment on Base. text: Big step for US stablecoin regulation. The OCC just became the first US regulator to finalize rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. The rules cover reserves, redemption, custody and capital requirements for banks and approved non-bank firms issuing dollar stablecoins. They take effect on January 18, 2027. Issuers still cannot pay interest, but the OCC dropped a proposed presumption against rewards paid through third parties, which drew criticism from the American Bankers Association. Clearer rules usually mean more institutions willing to build. $USDC #Stablecoins #GENIUSAct #CryptoNews

text: Position sizing under uncertainty: risk a fixed percentage of capital per trade, not a fixed dollar amount. If BTC is at $80,372 and you risk 1% of a $10,000 account, your stop-loss distance determines position size, not the asset price. A wider stop means a smaller position; a tighter stop means a larger one. This keeps drawdowns comparable across BTC, ETH, or SOL regardless of volatility. The trade-off is that tight stops can get shaken out by normal crypto noise, while wide stops require tiny sizes that may feel meaningless. Size for the worst case, not the best case. Observation: BTC is down 3.3% over 7 days per current market data. Interpretation: sizing rules matter most when prices move against you.

text: Open interest is one of the most cited yet misunderstood metrics in crypto derivatives. It measures the total number of unsettled futures or perpetual contracts outstanding across an exchange. Unlike spot volume, open interest does not tell you whether traders are bullish or bearish; it only tells you how much capital is currently at risk in open positions. A durable framework for reading open interest starts with three steps. First, establish the baseline. Open interest should always be evaluated against price action and funding rates. Rising open interest alongside rising price suggests new capital is entering long positions, which can confirm trend strength. text: Most crypto education focuses on price charts. A more durable lens is operational risk: who holds the keys, who can fail, and what breaks when they do. Use three buckets. 1. Custody risk: self-custody means you bear key management; third-party custody shifts it to the platform but adds counterparty exposure. 2. Counterparty risk: the borrower, exchange, or issuer may not return your funds. 3. Operational risk: code bugs, upgrade failures, and security delays can halt or drain systems even when prices are stable. Concrete example: Ethereum recently delayed the Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet after ChainSecurity flagged 13 real-world smart contracts potentially affected by gas changes. text: Drawdowns are unavoidable in crypto, but traders often confuse two different dimensions of risk: depth and time. Depth measures how far price falls from peak to trough, usually expressed as a percentage. Time measures how long price stays below that peak before recovering. A framework that separates the two can help you size positions, set stop logic, and manage psychology without relying on market predictions. Depth is intuitive. If an asset drops from 100 to 60, the drawdown depth is 40 percent. Time is less discussed but often more damaging. If that same asset takes six months to return to 100, the opportunity cost and emotional strain can exceed the price decline itself. In crypto, deep drawdowns are common, but prolonged sideways or choppy recoveries are equally common and often overlooked. A concrete example comes from recent market data.
